intro: OpenAI's GPT-6 launch headlines a busy day, while Brussels finalizes AI liability rules and inference hardware keeps pulling money.

must_know.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6 with real-time reasoning
must_know.summary: OpenAI announced GPT-6, its next flagship model, with real-time reasoning aimed at agent workloads.
must_know.why_it_matters: Sets the bar every other lab will be measured against this quarter.

must_know.title: EU parliament approves final AI liability rules
must_know.summary: EU lawmakers approved liability rules covering high-risk AI deployments, ending a two-year negotiation.
must_know.why_it_matters: Anyone shipping AI features into the EU now has concrete liability exposure.

must_know.title: Chipmaker Cerebra raises $400M for wafer-scale inference
must_know.summary: Cerebra closed a $400M round to scale its wafer-scale inference chips.
must_know.why_it_matters: Investors keep betting inference, not training, is the next hardware bottleneck.

research.title: Scaling sparse attention to 100M context
research.summary: A research note describes sparse attention kernels that extend usable context windows toward 100M tokens.

continuing.title: US expands chip export restrictions to inference GPUs
continuing.summary: The US extended chip export restrictions to cover inference GPUs.
continuing.update_delta: Inference GPUs were added to the restricted list, expanding yesterday's training-chip rules.
